# Results — Study 862 (Real Earnings Management)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — a
**Roychowdhury (2006) real-earnings-management proxy** (abnormally HIGH production + abnormally
LOW discretionary expense) **predicts forward stock returns**. Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Prices fingerprint `e443c0a5d730`
(yfinance daily adjusted closes); events cache = 630 (ticker, filing) rows.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Universe | **44** large US manufacturers / hardware / pharma / industrials (fixed, current survivors); **32** clear the ≥6-quarter usable-panel bar |
| Signal source | SEC EDGAR XBRL `companyconcept`: Revenues, CostOfRevenue/COGS, SG&A, R&D (flows) + InventoryNet, Assets (instants); de-duplicated on period end, earliest filing kept |
| Panel | **630** firm-quarters, period ends **2009-07-31 → 2026-03-31**, stamped with the **10-Q/10-K filing date** (point-in-time; no look-ahead) |
| Prices | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, sliced to 2026-06-30 |
| Primary signal | `rem = ab_prod − ab_disx` — the residuals of Roychowdhury's normal-production and normal-discretionary-expense models (higher ⇒ more real management: overproduce **and** cut R&D/SG&A) |
| Primary test | calendar-time monthly long-short: rank fresh signals into **terciles**, long top / short bottom, earn **next** month's return (one execution lag); decisive stat = **Newey-West (6-lag) t** |
| Costs | one-way × NAV × monthly turnover on both legs + annualised borrow on the short leg |

**Coverage caveat (first-class).** XBRL quarterly *flow* tags are sparse for the **fiscal fourth
quarter** (10-Ks disclose the full year, not Q4), R&D is missing for several consumer names
(GLW, ABT, GD, LMT, KMB, F never yield a usable panel), and the pre-2009 XBRL era is empty — so
only **32 of 44** names clear the ≥6-quarter bar and the monthly cross-section averages ≈17.
**Two modelling caveats:** the normal-expense benchmark coefficients are fit on the **full pooled
panel** (a mild in-sample look-ahead in the *benchmark*, not the signal; the sort trades the
cross-sectional rank), and with 32 names we **pool across industries** rather than run
Roychowdhury's per-industry-year regressions. No survivorship correction: the basket is current
survivors — named on the Signal axis.

## Headline — the forward-return long-short (does REM predict returns?)

Monthly rebalanced tercile long-short on `rem` (long high-REM / short low-REM), one execution lag,
2009-11 → 2026-03 (**153 months**, avg cross-section 17.1 names):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| long-short mean | **−9.2 bps/month** (−1.10%/yr, gross) |
| one-sample *t* | −0.21 |
| **Newey-West (6-lag) *t*** | **−0.16** |
| Sharpe (gross, ann.) | −0.06 |
| monthly hit rate | 46% |
| long leg / short leg | +179.6 / +188.8 bps/month |

The point estimate is a **near-perfect zero** (−0.16 HAC *t*). The literature predicts high-REM
firms *under*-perform, so the faintly-negative sign is at least in the right direction — but it is
**statistically indistinguishable from nothing**, and the specification is **not even sign-stable**:
switching the signal-staleness window from 200 to 120 days flips it to **+75.3 bps/mo, NW *t* =
+1.82** (opposite sign, near-significant), and the two REM components disagree — `ab_prod` alone is
−5.5 bps (NW *t* = −0.09), `ab_disx` alone is +30.7 bps (NW *t* = +0.69). A signal whose sign
depends on the staleness knob is noise, not an edge.

## Cross-check — pooled event drift (tercile sort by REM)

Bucket all (ticker, filing) events by `rem`; top-minus-bottom forward drift, entered one day after
the filing:

| horizon | n | top | bottom | long-short | one-sample *t* | win | placebo *p* (2-sided) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 21 d (≈1 m) | 630 | +1.70% | +1.26% | **+0.44%** | +0.63 | 46% | 0.53 |
| 63 d (≈1 q) | 629 | +4.65% | +5.52% | **−0.87%** | −0.62 | 47% | 0.49 |
| 126 d (≈2 q) | 628 | +10.16% | +10.45% | **−0.28%** | −0.14 | 45% | 0.88 |

Flat and **sign-flipping across horizons** (+0.44% at 1m, −0.87% at 1q). The tercile means are
**non-monotone** (63 d: +5.52% / +3.39% / +4.65% low→high — the *middle* third is the worst), no
horizon's *t* exceeds ±0.63, and the two-sided label-shuffle placebo *p* sits at **0.49–0.88** — a
random tercile split matches or beats the real one roughly every other draw. There is **no
forward-return sort** in this signal on this tape.

## Era split — the sign is not even stable across regimes

Calendar long-short, split at 2015-01-01:

| era | months | mean | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2010-2014 | 62 | **+69.5 bps** | +1.02 |
| 2015-2026 | 91 | **−62.8 bps** | −0.79 |

The long-short is **positive early and negative late** and insignificant in both halves — the
regimes cancel to the ≈0 full-sample number. This is the fingerprint of noise, not of an edge that
decayed: there was never a stable sign to decay from.

## The mechanism, too, is absent — REM does **not** foreshadow a gross-margin reversal

Pooled OLS of the **forward change in gross margin** (`next_gm − gm`) on REM (n = 339 matched
events). The value-destruction story predicts a **negative** slope (overproduction inflates
current margin, which must reverse):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| slope *b* | **+0.057** (wrong sign vs the reversal prediction) |
| *t* (iid-pooled) | +1.36 |
| R² | 0.005 |
| Pearson correlation | +0.074 |
| forward Δ gross margin, top-REM tercile | +0.56 pp |
| forward Δ gross margin, bottom-REM tercile | +0.08 pp |
| tercile spread | +0.48 pp |

Not only is the *return* claim a null — the *operating-reversal* mechanism is **not detected**
either: the slope is tiny, insignificant, and points the *wrong way* (R² = 0.005). On this small,
industry-pooled quarterly panel the abnormal-production residual does not predict a subsequent
gross-margin give-back. (Consistent with the modelling caveats — pooled-industry residuals are
noisy — this is a *non-detection*, not a refutation of Roychowdhury's original industry-year
finding.)

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic price + REM-signal panel with a TUNABLE planted lead (high-REM names drift up); no
network. Detector = the primary calendar long-short NW *t*.

| world | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **12 seeds** | mean **+0.31** (sd 0.78), \|t\| ≥ 2 in **0/12** seeds |
| planted edge = 0.15 (seed 862) | **+20.28** (mean +874.2 bps/month) |

The detector averages ≈0 on the null (never a false HAC crossing in twelve seeds) and lights up
hard on a planted lead. The real-tape NW *t* = −0.16 is therefore a genuine null, not a broken
pipeline. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of a real-tape stamp.)*

## Tradability — the timer

Calendar long-short net of one-way costs × turnover (both legs) + short-leg borrow (monthly
turnover ≈ 0.16):

| cost (one-way) | borrow (ann.) | net mean | ~ann. | Newey-West *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 bps | 50 bps | −9.0 bps/mo | −1.08%/yr | −0.16 | −0.06 |
| 20 bps | 100 bps | −8.8 bps/mo | −1.05%/yr | −0.16 | −0.06 |

There is nothing to cost: the gross edge is already a zero (a slightly *negative* zero). No
paycheck.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The forward-return long-short on the REM proxy is a **flat null**: primary
  Newey-West *t* = **−0.16** (one-sample −0.21), the pooled event drift is **flat, sign-flipping
  and non-monotone** (placebo *p* ≈ 0.5–0.9), the sign **is not stable** across the staleness knob
  (200 d: −9.2 bps; 120 d: +75.3 bps) or across eras (+69.5 bps pre-2015, −62.8 bps post), and the
  two components disagree. No robustness, no certification, no stable sign — the desk's definition
  of `NONE`.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A zero gross edge (NW *t* < 1, negative) cannot be traded; net of
  realistic long-short costs + borrow it is −0.16 *t*, Sharpe ≈ −0.06. No paycheck.
- **"Does REM foreshadow an operating reversal?" — NOT DETECTED.** The forward gross-margin change
  regresses on REM with a tiny, insignificant, **wrong-signed** slope (+0.057, *t* = +1.36, R² =
  0.005). On this industry-pooled EDGAR panel the mechanism is not observable — a first-class
  non-detection, honestly stamped, not a claim that Roychowdhury was wrong.

**Fingerprint `e443c0a5d730`** (prices; events cache 630 rows, 32 names, 2009-07-31 → 2026-03-31,
as-of 2026-06-30).
